claims.text: The investigated alloy has composition Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7.
Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is single-phase BCC after holding at 1100 °C.
Al atoms diffuse rapidly during cooling from the high-temperature BCC state.
Local Al enrichment nucleates nanoscale B2-ordered precipitates.
B2 precipitates alter the local chemical-potential landscape.
B2 precipitates lower the barrier to subsequent L12 gamma-prime formation.
The formation of B2 acts as a structural mediator controlling the eventual combination of B2, gamma-prime, and residual BCC phases.
Al clustering modifies local composition fields in a way that favors L12 gamma-prime ordering at lower temperatures.
Cooling at approximately 1 °C/s will produce a higher B2 volume fraction than cooling at more than 100 °C/s.
Slow-cooled specimens will develop more subsequent gamma-prime precipitates than rapid-quenched specimens.
Rapidly quenched specimens will remain largely single-phase BCC.
A quench faster than 100 °C/s from 1100 °C to room temperature will retain homogeneous BCC without B2 or gamma-prime.
The proposed mechanism applies when the Al concentration is at least 7 at.%, the alloy cools through 900–300 °C, and no external stress is applied.
The proposed mechanism does not apply if cooling is interrupted above 900 °C.
Below 7 at.% Al, there is insufficient Al to form B2 clusters.
Failure of slow cooling to cause a statistically significant increase in B2 and/or gamma-prime fraction relative to rapid quenching is designated as a falsification result.

contradictions.description: The intervention and experimental design cool both groups only to 300 °C, whereas the stated baseline is a quench to room temperature. Thus, the nominal baseline is not exactly the rapid-cooling condition implemented in the controlled comparison.
